explanation: Modern computer systems utilize a memory hierarchy to bridge the speed gap between CPU and main memory.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of storage with varying speeds and capacities (registers, L1 cache, L2 cache, L3 cache, main memory, disk).  Understanding and exploiting this hierarchy is crucial for optimizing program performance, as accessing data from faster levels significantly reduces execution time.  Techniques involve data locality (temporal and spatial) to maximize cache hits and minimize costly accesses to slower memory levels.
